today.text: The Utah monolith, built sometime in 2016 is discovered by state biologists of the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources.
NASA launches the MAVEN probe to Mars.
Pope Tawadros II of Alexandria becomes the 118th Pope of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria.

today.text: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court rules 4–3 in Goodridge v. Department of Public Health that the state's ban on same-sex marriage is unconstitutional and gives the state legislature 180 days to change the law making Massachusetts the first state in the United States to grant marriage rights to same-sex couples.
pages: Goodridge v. Department of Public Health

today.text: Iraq disarmament crisis: United Nations weapons inspectors led by Hans Blix arrive in Iraq.
At Texas A&M University, the Aggie Bonfire collapses killing 12 students and injuring 27 others.
A fire occurs on a train traveling through the Channel Tunnel from France to England causing several injuries and damaging approximately 500 metres (1,600 ft) of tunnel.
In the United States, the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is approved by the House of Representatives.
In South Africa, 21 political parties approve a new constitution, expanding voting rights and ending white minority rule.
Shiite Muslim kidnappers in Lebanon release Anglican Church envoys Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland.

random.title: Loopy (film)
random.extract: Loopy is a 2004 film written and directed by Seth Michael Donsky.  It is an adaptation of a short story by Ruth Rendell. Loopy screened at the Palm Springs International Festival of Short Films, the Cinequest Film Festival and the Clermont-Ferrand International Short Film Festival.  Loopy currently airs in rotation on the Independent Film Channel. The tagline for the film is "A sheep in wolf's clothing!"

entry.title: Milky Way versus Aurora
entry.summary:
Explanation: Are these two giant arches battling for control of the sky? No, but it sure looks like it! The arch on the left is the central band of our Milky Way Galaxy, an ancient system of stars, gas, and dust that predates our Earth and is very far away. The arch on the right, by contrast, is an auroral ribbon that is only hours old, composed of energized atoms and molecules, and is close by -- right in Earth's upper atmosphere. These chance-superposed titans have our Sun in common, a stellar member of the Milky Way that ejects energetic particles which create auroras. Far behind the middle of the auroral arch is the Big Dipper. Even farther in the distance is the Andromeda galaxy -- the bright spot near the top of the frame, just left of center. The featured image was taken about a month ago from Kvaløya in northern Norway.

Tomorrow's picture: open space
